contract: ABNAHME.md §113 (finding_id, severity, criterion_ids, base_revision, platform, repro_steps, expected, actual, files_symbols, evidence, cause_or_hypothesis, fix_hint, retest). §112 defines P0-P3.

state_vocabulary.open: confirmed defect, no fix applied or fix incomplete (residual risk documented)
state_vocabulary.suppressed: the originally reported attack shape is proven gone by a fresh repro (retake), but a sibling/bypass shape remains and is listed in the same entry or a *b entry
state_vocabulary.fixed_retested: fix landed (named commit/commit-range) and a fresh independent repro on the fixed tree shows the defect shape is gone
state_vocabulary.pass_negative: reviewed and found to be sound; recorded so the negative result is auditable (never evidence for another criterion)

criteria_cross_check.command: .venv/bin/python - <<'PY' (see docs/ABNAHME-STATUS.md §Verification; every criterion_id below was asserted to exist in the 97-id register and the script exits non-zero otherwise)

findings.base_revision: f9442a8 (round 1) / fixed at 5a86bc4, retested at a6f03df
repro_steps: Run /tmp/gv_review_sec/probe_briefs.py case 3 against src/godsv/subagent_briefs.py: create brief (owner=w1, epoch=1), takeover to w2/epoch=2, call on_timeout(assignment, owner='w1', owner_epoch=1).
Round 1: unfenced on_timeout accepted the stale settle (`unfenced on_timeout accepted: True timed_out_partial`).
Retake: same probe pointed at the fixed tree (PYTHONPATH=$GV/src) -> out_sec01_12.txt.
findings.expected: Only the current (owner, owner_epoch) pair may settle a brief; a stale/unknown caller is refused.
findings.actual: Round 1: on_timeout took no owner/epoch at all and never called check_fencing; any caller could close a live brief as timed_out_partial and the real owner's later report_result was rejected as already_settled. Retake: refused (unknown_owner), replay after settle refused (already_settled), fresh owner accepted (delivered).
files_symbols: src/godsv/subagent_briefs.py::BriefCoordinator.on_timeout (L234-247 round 1; L234-258 now, calls check_fencing L252)
findings.cause_or_hypothesis: on_timeout was written as an internal helper with public framing and no fencing; report_result fenced the same transition correctly.
findings.fix_hint: Route on_timeout through check_fencing(brief, owner=..., owner_epoch=...) like report_result.
findings.retest: PASS — fresh repro on the fixed tree: stale owner refused, replay refused, current owner accepted. Residual: the refusal reason surfaces as `unknown_owner` rather than `stale_epoch` (cosmetic).

repro_steps: Run /tmp/gv_review_sec/probe_briefs.py case 4 (deterministic interleaving report_result reads brief -> takeover bumps epoch -> report_result compares epoch -> accept), also looped with two threads.
Re-checked at a6f03df: no coordinator-level lock was introduced in the fix range.
findings.expected: takeover and result acceptance are mutually exclusive: a result validated before the takeover either completes atomically or is fenced out.
findings.actual: check_fencing returns a reason string (no accepted-result snapshot); epoch check and status write are separate unlocked steps and BriefCoordinator has no lock, so a racing check that ran just before the bump can still write the terminal status after the takeover.
findings.cause_or_hypothesis: epoch check + write are not a single compare-and-set; no lock in the coordinator.
findings.fix_hint: One coordinator-level threading.Lock; re-read brief.owner_epoch inside the lock immediately before the status write.
findings.retest: not_run — no fix landed in the reviewed range; the narrow race needs a looped two-thread harness as the retest.

repro_steps: Run /tmp/gv_review_sec/probe_briefs.py case 5: abort_all() returns the side_effects_unknown list; inspect the run audit trail.
Round 1 probe_store2.py also persists a fabricated BriefDecision(accepted=True, outcome='delivered') from owner='fakeworker'/epoch=999 (that half is now closed, see GV2-SEC-12).
findings.expected: parent abort records which briefs had external_may_have_started and persists that decision; the integrator is not free to drop it.
findings.actual: abort_all returns the unknown list but no audit event for the abort is written and nothing enforces that the integrator calls record_brief_result per brief — an aborted brief with unknown side effects can leak silently. Still true at HEAD: `grep -rn 'record_abort' src/godsv` finds nothing.
findings.cause_or_hypothesis: the fencing lives only in BriefCoordinator; the persistence seam has no abort path.
findings.fix_hint: Add record_abort(...) writing the unknown-IDs list into the audit detail, and call it from the abort path.
findings.retest: not_run — no abort audit exists at HEAD; smallest retest is an audit-row assertion after abort_all.

repro_steps: Run /tmp/gv_review_sec/probe_briefs.py case 6: build a valid SubagentBrief, then brief.allowed_write_paths.clear() / brief.worker_kind = 'other_kind' after construction, then hand it to the coordinator.
Check at HEAD whether enqueue_brief re-validates.
findings.expected: a brief with an empty write scope (or a code worker without a worktree) must not be accepted, even if mutated after construction.
findings.actual: validate_brief runs only in __post_init__ (L70-71); no re-validation at the persistence seam. `run_supervisor.py::enqueue_brief` (L1035-1097 at HEAD) checks isinstance only and serialises the live dataclass — post-validation mutation lands in the payload.
findings.cause_or_hypothesis: dataclass contract validated once; no freeze and no re-validation.
findings.fix_hint: Call validate_brief(brief) again inside enqueue_brief before serialisation, and/or make SubagentBrief frozen with allowed_write_paths as tuple.
findings.retest: not_run — needs an assertion that a mutated brief is refused by enqueue_brief.

findings.base_revision: f9442a8 (round 1) / fixed at 5a86bc4, retested at a6f03df
repro_steps: Round 1: /tmp/gv_review_sec/probe_budget.py — reserve nothing and call spend(role, 199) in a loop (200 floor spends, 39 800 of 150 000 tokens; 369 543 across all roles in probe3).
Retake: /tmp/gv_review_sec2/r_sec05_cap_mix.py — floor-spend ramp at the new cap plus a 2-thread race at the cap boundary and a 4-thread mixed reserve/floor invariant run.
findings.expected: the per-call small-spend floor is a convenience for occasional small spends, never an unlimited alternative account; the aggregate reservation-less spend is capped.
findings.actual: Round 1: the floor check was per-call only (`amount > self._small_floor`) with no cumulative cap. Retake: cap enforced inside the same lock — `cap refused after 2 floor-spends (400 tokens): cumulative reservation-less spend 600 exceeds the unreserved cap 500 (5% of 10000)`; 2-thread race accepted=1 refused=1; 4-thread mixed invariant spent+reserved<=limit held.
findings.cause_or_hypothesis: spend() treated each unreserved call as independent with no aggregate counter for floor-class spends.
findings.fix_hint: (applied) cumulative `st._unreserved_spent` per role plus a configured unreserved cap derived from the role limit.
findings.retest: PASS — floor ramp stops with a structured BudgetExceeded at the cap; atomicity confirmed under 2- and 4-thread races. Residual: reservation-churn bypass (GV2-SEC-05b).

findings.fix_hint: Make cancel=True explicitly no-op with a comment, or implement the reversal against an actual-spend ledger keyed by reservation id.

repro_steps: Read BudgetAccount._lock (single, L130) vs TokenBucket._lock (per-bucket, L72) and inspect dump_ledger (L273-281): `entries = list(self._ledger)` is taken without the account lock.

findings.actual: the dump can interleave entries from two logical operations; no crash (CPython list() is atomic enough) but the dump can show an order that never happened.

findings.fix_hint: Take self._lock around the snapshot in dump_ledger.

repro_steps: Round 1: /tmp/gv_review_sec/probe_store2.py — construct SubagentBrief(owner='fakeworker', owner_epoch=999) and call record_brief_result('r1', brief2, BriefDecision(accepted=True, outcome='delivered')).

findings.expected: only results fenced by the owning coordinator are persistable.
findings.actual: Round 1: the store took brief+decision at face value and persisted `delivered` with a trusted audit line (return True). Retake: rejected BEFORE the DB write (`forged-owner store record return: False persisted status: created`) and audited with the full fencing detail (claimed/persisted owner+epoch, reason=fencing_mismatch).
findings.cause_or_hypothesis: no stamping/cross-check between coordinator and store; decision.accepted was trusted self-attestation.
findings.fix_hint: (applied) check claimed owner/epoch against the PERSISTED brief payload, plus a monotonic-epoch fence and an outcome-lie rank gate.

repro_steps: /tmp/gv_review_sec2/r_sec12_outcome_smuggle.py: a caller holding the GENUINE (owner, owner_epoch) mutates the in-memory brief.status to 'delivered' and hands a matching BriefDecision to the store. Coordinator truth was `timed_out_empty`; the store persisted `delivered` + outcome=delivered and the audit shows a successful subagent_brief_result with no contradiction marker.
findings.expected: the store derives the persisted outcome from the coordinator's own state, not from caller-supplied dataclass fields.
findings.actual: at HEAD the store compares the decision's outcome against `brief.status` via a truth-rank table (_TRUTH_RANK: delivered 3 / timed_out_partial 2 / timed_out_empty 1 / aborted 0) but `brief.status` itself is caller-supplied, so a caller who also bumps the brief status passes the rank gate.
findings.cause_or_hypothesis: two sources of truth (coordinator memory vs the store) with no single choke point; the rank gate narrows but does not close the seam.
findings.fix_hint: Have record_brief_result accept the Coordinator (or its returned BriefDecision) instead of caller-built fixtures — one choke point.
findings.retest: not_run — retest is re-running r_sec12_outcome_smuggle.py and expecting a refusal or an audited contradiction marker.

findings.base_revision: f9442a8 (round 1 P1) / partially fixed at 5a86bc4, retested at a6f03df (downgraded)
repro_steps: Round 1: /tmp/gv_review_sec/probe_rf06_pair.py case 1 — preserved text containing `gsk_live_...` was reintroduced verbatim.
Retake: /tmp/gv_review_sec2/r_sec13_14_rf06.py + out_prefix_unit.txt / out_rf07_redact_unit.txt — probe the delegation target directly.
findings.expected: text reintroduced through the preserve channel passes the engine's secret redaction.
findings.actual: `_rf06_redact` is now wired in at the reintegrate site (host-overlay/patch_rf06_compression_preserve.py L72-80, delegating to `agent.redact.redact_sensitive_text(force=True)` when importable) — the SITE is covered, but the delegate misses four shapes: (1) `gsk_live_<underscored body>` (pattern `gsk_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}` rejects `_`), (2) `vnc://user:pass@host` userinfo, (3) secrets split across two lines, (4) base64-encoded blobs. Probe: `LEAK gsk: True`, `LEAK vnc-pass: True`.
findings.cause_or_hypothesis: the delegation target's prefix list is narrower than the credential shapes in use; no entropy/line-continuation pass.
findings.fix_hint: Widen the redactor (allow `_` in `gsk_` bodies, cover `vnc://` userinfo, join line-splits before scanning, add a base64/entropy heuristic) or persist hashes instead of literal text.
findings.retest: PARTIAL — site covered, four leak shapes reproduced on the fixed tree; treated as a remaining limitation (P2).

repro_steps: /tmp/gv_review_sec/probe_rf06_skew.py — map all four `return messages` early-exit sites inside compress() that skip reintegrate (insufficient_messages, no_compressible_window, empty_post_handoff_window, abort-on-summary-failure) and inspect `_rf06_preserve` afterwards.
findings.expected: after an aborted compression attempt the preserve snapshot is cleared or paired to a successful reintegrate.
findings.actual: `_rf06_preserve` is set before the analyse step and only consumed on the success path; on abort paths it stays armed with the previous window's content. Impact is bounded (the next real attempt overwrites it before use; there is no in-tree consumer), so this was downgraded P1→P2, but a future reordering or an external reader reintroduces stale rows silently.
findings.cause_or_hypothesis: snapshot armed at collection time, not cleared on the abort paths.
findings.fix_hint: Set self._rf06_preserve = [] (or emit telemetry) in each early-return path.
findings.retest: not_run — retest is asserting the attribute is empty after each abort path.
